chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from ʿAlī, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said:
I said: A man applies dye while he is in janabah? He said, “There is no harm.” And about a woman applying dye while she is menstruating, he said, “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it; no legal objection
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye, especially to the hair or with henna

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to apply dye while in janabah or during menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that applying dye is permissible for a man in janabah and for a woman during hayd. It indicates that such grooming is not prohibited by the state of ritual impurity or menstruation.
